relevance_note: This is a case report of a monogenic type-1 interferonopathy treated with anifrolumab, but the patient's variant is in another gene, not TNFAIP3: "a homozygous missense variant in the DNASE2 gene (NM_001375.2:c.1040G>A, p.Cys347Tyr)".
method_note: Read the whole file (header, text, Table I, figure legend, references). No TNFAIP3 variant and no HA20/A20 haploinsufficiency diagnosis is reported anywhere, so no person is in scope; per extract_v6 'When the paper describes no in-scope person', reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant is false, only the publications row is filled, and the other four tables are empty. The only patient ("a 15-year-old boy", "our patient") carries a homozygous DNASE2 variant inherited from each parent; his mother (autoimmune hypothyroidism), his two parents and his healthy 7-year-old sibling are mentioned, but none of them is described in relation to a person with a TNFAIP3 variant or an HA20 diagnosis, so they get no rows. Had they been in scope, labels would be 'patient' (rule 5) and 'mother of patient' / 'parent of patient' / 'parent of patient 2' / 'sibling of patient' (rule 2). Table I lists only this patient's cell counts over time and is not a per-patient table; it contains no ' / ' stacked cells and no per-patient source-reference column. Contradictions noticed but not relevant here: the paper reports 'His spleen was noted to be mildly enlarged.' yet also says the case 'lacks hepatomegaly'; it says he 'technically met criteria for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis' while also stating 'His infectious and autoimmune histories were unremarkable throughout early childhood', and he was later 'diagnosed with autoimmune hypothyroidism'. No functional assay is reported for the DNASE2 variant itself (the assays concern the patient's interferon signature).
